why: efficientnet_b0 beats the served resnet18 on val (0.6917 vs 0.6500) AND on test (0.6700 vs 0.5750, both re-measured CPU fp32 by verify_retrain_gains.py --ckpt); TTA flag decided on val; converged in 19 epochs against the incumbent's 30, so the gain is not a training-budget artefact

efficientnet_b0 beats the served resnet18 on val by +0.0708 (0.8714 vs 0.8006 on a 1003-image val, i.e. 71 images - well outside the noise that makes breast undecidable) and on test by +0.0658 (0.8793 vs 0.8135), with macro-F1 up +0.0833; both re-measured CPU fp32 and reproducing exactly; TTA decided on val; both runs converged before their epoch caps so the gain is not a training-budget artefact

efficientnet_b0 with the v2 recipe beats the served v1 resnet18 at the SAME 64px resolution and the same 20k training subsample: val 0.9818 vs 0.9718 measured in one harness on 10,004 val images (a 100-image margin, not the 2-image ambiguity that makes breast undecidable), test 0.9545 vs 0.9440, macro-F1 0.9394 vs 0.9239, AUC 0.9975 vs 0.9957, and a smaller overfitting gap (+0.0328 vs +0.0455); re-measured CPU fp32 and reproduces exactly

efficientnet_b0 with geometry_safe augmentation at the SAME 64px resolution as the served v1: val 0.9941 vs 0.9883 measured in one harness on 2392 val images, test 0.9533 vs 0.9419, macro-F1 0.9477 vs 0.9353, smaller overfitting gap (+0.0460 vs +0.0571); re-measured CPU fp32 and reproduces exactly. The augmentation policy is the point - organc has kidney-left/right, lung-left/right and femur-left/right, and RandomHorizontalFlip relabels those images, which cost the served model 139 of its 477 errors

efficientnet_b0 @224 with the v2 recipe against the served v1 resnet18 @64: val 0.9924 vs 0.9796 measured in one harness on 1712 val images (~22 images), test 0.9883 vs 0.9787, macro-F1 0.9889, AUC 0.9994; re-measured CPU fp32 and reproduces exactly. Caveat recorded in TRAINING_LOG step 83: this run changed resolution, backbone and recipe together, so the gain is real and measured but not attributed to a single lever - blood smears are stained colour images, so 64 to 224 is likely the largest part of it
